paragraphs: Dryad provides ultra-early wildfire detection and autonomous drone systems for public and private forests. The sensors are meant to detect fires within minutes from ignition so firefighters can put them out before they spread out of control.

The fourth generation sensor combines VOC, CO and PM2.5 sensing to catch a fire as early as the smoldering phase. The units form a wireless environmental sensor network based on LoRaWAN. A patented distributed architecture is meant to allow large-scale deployments in areas without existing network coverage. A cloud platform handles deployment planning, operation, analytics and alerting for those networks. An observation drone is dispatched when a sensor detects a fire, and a second drone applies fire suppressant liquids to extinguish fires autonomously.

Beyond forest owners, the company pitches utility and grid operators on protection against liabilities. Published case studies include a fire in Lebanon stopped by early detection. The founders say they came to this work after several startups and exits in IT, electronics and telecommunications.

quote.text: When it comes to fighting wildfires, speed is everything.
